input_oneliner: 45M prior anterior MI, EF 35%, sudden-onset regular pounding heartbeat 20 min ago, HR 170, BP 104/68, lightheaded, mentating

reference_targets_freetext.item: Bedside hemodynamic stability: mentation, chest pain, dyspnea, peripheral perfusion (capillary refill, skin temperature)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Determines whether the next step is immediate cardioversion or diagnostic maneuvers

reference_targets_freetext.item: Jugular venous pulse for intermittent cannon a waves and variable intensity of S1 (AV dissociation)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Bedside signs of AV dissociation favor VT over SVT in a wide-complex tachycardia

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about prior similar episodes since youth and whether they stopped with breath-holding or straining
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Recurrent self-terminating episodes since young adulthood favor SVT; first event after MI favors VT

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about angina or dyspnea in the preceding days and adherence to beta-blocker or antiarrhythmic
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Ischemia and missed antiarrhythmic therapy are common VT triggers in a scarred ventricle

reference_targets_freetext.item: Modified Valsalva maneuver (REVERT: 15 s strain then supine with passive leg raise), only if stable and regular
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Terminates or unmasks SVT; failure to respond in a patient with scar raises VT probability

should_not_recommend: Adenosine or verapamil before the rhythm is seen on a 12-lead ECG in a patient with prior MI (treat wide-complex tachycardia as VT)
Carotid sinus massage without first auscultating for carotid bruits
Deferring bedside hemodynamic assessment until the ECG is printed

perturbation_pair.changed_feature: prior anterior MI with EF 35% -> no cardiac history, structurally normal heart
perturbation_pair.input_oneliner: 45M no cardiac history, sudden-onset regular pounding heartbeat 20 min ago, HR 170, BP 104/68, lightheaded, mentating
